 Judgment

These two appeals are preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the common judgment and award dated 3rd August 2016, passed in MVC no.1958/2012, on the file of the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Mandya.

sentences.text: 2. MFA No.8061/2016 is filed by the insurance company on the ground that the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
Whereas, MFA no.2005/2017 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation.

3. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the insurance company and learned counsel for the claimant and perused the materials on record.
NC: 2024:KHC:21383 4.
The learned counsel for the insurance company submits that the quantum of compensation awarded under various heads in on the higher side.
Therefore, seeks for reduction of compensation.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimant submits that the quantum of compensation awarded under various heads is on the lesser side.
Therefore, seeks for enhancement of compensation.

6. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under various heads is as follows:

4 Towards future medical expenses Rs. 30,000-00 5
Towards loss of income during laid Rs. 40,000-00 down period 6
Towards loss of future income due Rs.2,72,200-00 to permanent disability 7
Towards future amenities in the life Rs. 25,000-00 of the petitioner
8 Towards loss of mobile set and Rs. 6,500-00 damage to ladies finger Total Rs.5,99,861-00 7.
The occurrence of the accident, injuries sustained by the claimant and coverage of insurance are not in dispute.
From the medical evidence on record, it is proved that the claimant has suffered fracture of shaft of left femur and compound fracture in right leg.

Considering the injuries sustained, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering; medical expenses; conveyance,
nursing care, nourishment and other incidental expenses; future medical expenses; loss of income during laid up period ; future amenities; and towards loss of mobile set and damage to ladies finger,
is found to be adequate and sufficient and same does not call for interference.
9.
The claimant is an agriculturist, but he has not produced any relevant documents in proof of income.
In the absence of proof of income, the notional income ought to have been taken at Rs.7,000/- per month as per the notional income chart as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Therefore, the monthly income taken by the Tribunal at Rs.15,000/- is on the higher side and Rs.7,000/- would be just and proper.
The doctor has stated that the claimant has suffered 33% disability to the lower limb.
Considering the age, avocation and injuries sustained by the claimant, functional disability would be 11%, which is rightly NC: 2024:KHC:21383 taken by the Tribunal.
From the medical records produced, age of the claimant is 43 years and hence, the proper multiplier is '14'.
Therefore, compensation under the head of 'loss of future income due to permanent disability' is re-
assessed and quantified at Rs.1,29,360/- (Rs.7000 x 12 x 14 x 11%) as against Rs.2,77,200/- awarded by the Tribunal.
10. The Tribunal has granted interest at the rate of 9% per annum on the compensation amount.
The same is scaled down to 6% per annum.
11. In view of the above, claimant is entitled for compensation under various heads as follows:

In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER i) MFA no.8061/2016 filed by the insurance company is allowed in part.
ii) MFA no.2005/2017 filed by the claimant is dismissed.

iii) The claimant would be entitled to reduced compensation of Rs.4,52,021/-
(Rupees four lakhs fifty-two thousand and twenty-one only) as against Rs.5,99,861/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
The interest is scalled down from 9% per annum to 6% per annum.
iv) The impugned judgment and award dated 3rd August 2016, passed in MVC no.1958/2012, on the file of the II Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Mandya, is modified to the above extent.
